explanation: The Aberdeen Act did not invent a British claim over the Brazilian traffic; it enforced one that had been conceded thirty-five years earlier. The 1810 treaty is where Portugal first agreed to limit the importation of Africans and to consider abolishing the trade, and the Anglo-Brazilian convention of 1826 — the instrument the 1845 Act names in its own long title as the thing it amends — is that concession inherited by the new empire. `precondition-of`: without the promise there is nothing for the Act to be the enforcement of.
